title: Cargo cults building landing tracks

plain: Island peoples in the Pacific are said to have built landing strips to call back the aircraft that once came to them, a practice known as a cargo cult. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, saying cargo cults in French Polynesia build landing tracks for "presumably some alien craft to return" in a way rooted in their mythology. The author Peter Levenda tells it differently, describing how in the early 20th century and the Second World War "planes would land on islands in the South Pacific," with no mention of alien craft. A researcher named Jason Simosa repeats it as he heard it from Levenda, placing it in French Polynesia though he admits he is unsure of the geography; the point is that people may remember visitors from the sky in ritual and myth.
